headline: On the data/catalog lens the v5.0 Master Recipe solves a duplication problem our catalog does not have: 130 CUTS, **zero duplicate names**, and 61% of a cut's shipped bytes are cited fact (`src`/`order_svsmoke`/`order_smokesv`/`grillable`/`grt|grh|grz`) with another 19% already machine-derived by `equipment_map.py`. Only ~20% of a cut is hand-written "body", and inside that body only 33–57% of the cook parameters are predictable from category — so a category-keyed generic engine would be wrong on roughly half our catalog. Its §3.1/§3.3 tables carry no citations and contain at least three defects our own cited data refutes outright (chicken liver at 63–65 °C, the fish force-to-52 °C rule, and a cheese rule that blocks our shipped hot-smoked cream cheese). Two mechanisms are genuinely new and worth taking in adapted form — consumables quantities and a smoker smoke-intensity band — plus a handful of cheap annotation ideas.
isItSmarter:
**Worse on my lens, with two narrow exceptions.**

Its central claim — "אם תאסוף 100 מתכונים לעישון בריסקט, 95 מהם הם קומבינציות שונות של אותם משתנים בדיוק… במקום לשכפל מתכונים — לבנות מתכון-על" (§1.1) — is a diagnosis of a corpus we do not have. `python -c "collections.Counter(x['heb'] for x in data.CUTS)"` returns **zero duplicated names across 130 CUTS**. We store one brisket (`cut n=1`) with cited paths, not 100.

Where it claims we'd gain, I measured what we'd actually lose. Byte accounting of the built payload (post `build.py` merge of `sources.py` + `equipment_map.apply`):

| | total | cited fact | equip (derived) | hand body |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CUTS (130) | 310,487 | **189,699 (61%)** | 59,580 (19%) | 61,208 (20%) |
| SPECIALS (47) | 43,684 | 23,267 (53%) | 3,556 (8%) | 16,861 (39%) |
| MAKES (102) | 283,838 | 82,185 (29%) | 21,188 (7%) | 180,465 (64%) |

And within the CUTS body, how much a generic engine could derive from `cat` alone (% of items equal to their category's modal value):

`safe` 92% · `wrap` 98% · `coal` 72% · `mid` 65% · `sear` 59% · `smt` **57%** · `sot` 52% · `rest` 45% · `svt` **43%** · `tgt` **41%** · `smh` 39% · `svh` 34% · `soh` **33%** · `somid` 28% · `rub` **19%** (105 distinct values / 130 items).

Read that table against §3.1's promise. The one field the proposal is most confident about — the "Hardcoded" USDA safety layer — is the one field that IS ~category-constant (`safe`: 6 distinct values, 92% modal) and the one we already have fully cited. Everything the Master Recipe actually claims to *generate* (`P_CHAMBER_TEMP`, `P_TARGET_INT`, `P_TIME_LIMIT`) is 33–57% derivable. So the engine would be right where it adds nothing and wrong where it claims to add value.

Where it IS smarter than us, honestly: (a) **consumables quantity** (§6.4 kg fuel/hour, metres of butcher paper, ×1.2 buffer). Our approved `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-20-equipment-consumption-layer-design.md` §A3 models refuel *cadence* (D4) but no quantity anywhere; nothing in `app.js`'s inventory (~line 10049) derives a shopping quantity from cook hours. (b) The **loss/gain-of-attribute annotation** (`LOSS_OF_ATTR: ["BARK","SMOKE_AROMA"]`, §4.4) — naming what a path costs you is a real UX idea we have no equivalent of, and it carries no number so it cannot hurt safety.

Where we are plainly ahead and it is not close:
- **Our master-recipe model already exists, in the place where it pays.** MAKES is not 102 hand-typed recipes: ~696 source lines (`data.py` 534–960 + `sausages_new.py`, 54 `SG()` calls + `b_fresh`/`b_emul`/`b_pastrami`/`b_shawarma`/`b_salumi`) expand to 283 KB of JSON — a ~400:1 parameterization ratio. We adopted the pattern where recipes genuinely are variable-substitutions and declined it where they are cited singletons. That is the correct discrimination, and the proposal does not make it.
- **Equipment derivation.** §5.2's `MenuItems.area_required_cm2` is an *input the caller must supply*; it never says how. `equipment_map.py:137` derives it: `SHAPE_CM2_PER_KG = {slab:240, roast:150, pieces:330, bird:200, long:200}`, calibrated against a real 45×28 cm packer brisket ≈1,300 cm² ≈ 55% of a 2,400 cm² shelf. §5.2's `DetailedEquipment` (4 types, `shelves_count`, `shelf_area_cm2`, `supports_hanging`) is a strict subset of `EQUIP_CATS` (app.js:34–102: 8 smoker types with sourced `areaCm2` defaults — the cabinet 7900 cm² is a documented 3-model average — plus `maxC`, `canHang`, `hooks`, `waterPan`, outer + shelf dimensions).
- **Glaze timing is already shipped.** §4.2/Rule 3 wants "delay glaze to the last 15–20 minutes". `app.js:1287` and `app.js:7272` already schedule every `kind==='glaze'` seasoning at `lastCook.end − 15 min` with "10-15 דק׳ אחרונות, בשכבות" — unconditionally, which is *safer* than the proposal's `IF P_CHAMBER_TEMP > 140°C` gate.
- **Rule 1 is already shipped and finer-grained.** `methodRules(c)` (app.js:989) branches produce / offal / gizzard / `doneness` / collagen, and for collagen cuts sets `needsCookFor:'grill', invalid:[['grill']]` — grill legal only as a finish. `validCombo` (app.js:1041) enforces it. The proposal's Rule 1 is one undifferentiated `collagen_level === "HIGH"` flag with no source for how HIGH is assigned.

Two corrections to `OUR-SYSTEM-BRIEF.md` while I was verifying it (code wins): (1) §1 says "354 תיבולים" — the **shipped** count is **301**; 354 is the raw 138 + 216 sum before `build.py:14-18` dedupes 53 by id/eng/heb. `seasoning_tags` covers 289 of the 301. (2) §1 says "279 ציטוטים" — there are 279 recipe *citation blocks* containing **1,008 individual `{ref,url,note}` objects, 595 distinct refs, 193 distinct URLs**. The larger number is the real migration surface.

adopt.item: Per-path LOSS_OF_ATTR / GAIN_OF_ATTR annotation (§4.4: `SET LOSS_OF_ATTR = ["BARK","SMOKE_AROMA"]`, `SET GAIN_OF_ATTR = ["HIGHER_JUICINESS"]`)
adopt.why: Pure prose metadata carrying no number, so it cannot touch a safety value or a DoD-10 invariant. It answers the one question our path list currently cannot: 'what do I give up if I pick sv→smoke instead of smoke-only'. We already enumerate 120 `order_svsmoke` + 13 `order_smokesv` paths and label them, but a user choosing between them sees only temps and hours.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: New optional `loses`/`gains` string arrays on the `itemPaths(meta)` entries (app.js:4175-4189), sourced from a per-path field in `sources.py` alongside the existing `ref`/`url`/`note`. Rendered by CP2's path-selection panel (the unbuilt half of `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-cooking-paths-single-source-design.md`). All strings must go through `L(he,en)` with static literals or Guard A fails.

adopt.item: Rule 6's structural half: skin-bearing items get a derived skin-scoring prep step AND a mandatory sear/grill finish stage in the pipeline
adopt.why: It is a shape rule, not a number, so it is safe to derive. Today `cut n=48` Duck Breast carries `mid:"חריטת עור"` and `cut n=9` Goose Breast carries `mid:"ייבוש"` as free prose that `itemStages` renders but nothing reasons over — no rule guarantees a skin item ends on a sear. That is exactly the `deriveRequires` pattern `equipment_map.py` already uses for casing/grind/cure.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: `equipment_map.cut_equip()` (equipment_map.py:248) already gates the grill path on `sear != 'לא'`; add a `has_skin` derivation from the existing shape/name regexes (`_SHAPE_WORDS`, equipment_map.py:148) and surface it as an `equip.spec` key, consumed by `itemStages` (app.js:4093) the same way `m.combo.includes('grill')` already appends a finish stage.

adopt.item: Explicit negative (BLOCK) pairing rules in the flavor layer (§7: `BLOCK: Fish` on the Texas profile)
adopt.why: Our seasoning→protein join is positive-only: `SEASONINGS[].cats` lists 12 protein categories (`עוף` 109, `בקר` 71, `חזיר` 52, `טלה` 40, `דג` 38, `ירקות` 30, ...). Absence-means-no is not the same as a stated block, and the AI seasoning recommender (app.js:10375, 'בחר id מהרשימה בלבד') has no negative constraint to ground on. A small explicit block list is cheap and closes an AI-grounding hole.
adopt.whereItPlugsIn: New `blocks:[cat,...]` array in `seasoning_tags.py` (289 entries today), merged in `build.py:20-25` next to the existing `flavor`/`base`/`heat` tags; consumed by the seasoning picker filters (app.js:1483) and the AI prompt at app.js:10375.

adapt.item: Consumables rate model (§6.4: offset ~1.5 kg wood/h, charcoal cabinet ~0.8 kg + 2 chunks/h, pellet ~1.0/2.0 kg/h, butcher paper ~1.5 m per wrapped cut, `safetyBuffer = 1.2`)
adapt.why: Genuinely absent from us. `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-20-equipment-consumption-layer-design.md` §A3 gives refuel *cadence* per device type but never a quantity, and the shopping/inventory list (app.js ~10049, groups 'עצים'/'מלח וסוכר'/'ריפוי') has no path from cook-hours to kilograms. A 12-hour brisket (`soh:'12'`) on an offset is the single most common 'did I buy enough fuel' failure and we answer it nowhere.
adapt.whatMustChange: Every number must be replaced. Not one of these five figures carries a source, and they are the kind of figure that varies 2-3× with ambient temperature, pit insulation and fire management. Land them as `EQUIP_CATS` smoker-type properties (app.js:34-79, alongside `areaCm2`/`maxC`) with the same treatment `areaCm2` got — a stated, documented derivation (the cabinet 7900 cm² comment at app.js:39-45 is the template) — or as measured owner values. Then give it a real consumer before shipping (DoD-5 / `no-inert-shipment`): the shopping list and the `equipPlan` seam, not a stored field nothing reads. The ×1.2 buffer is fine and needs no citation because it is an explicit stated margin, not a claim about the world.

adapt.item: Smoke-intensity coefficient per smoker type (§4.3: offset 1.5, charcoal cabinet 1.2, pellet 0.8, electric/gas 0.6)
adapt.why: We already ship smoker-type-specific *advice* — `lang/_extracted.json` keys 0-4 are per-cooker guidance ('אופסט: נהל אש קטנה ונקייה…', 'פלט: שגר-ושכח. לעשן חזק יותר — הוסף צינור/מבוך עשן…') — but nothing quantifies the difference, so nothing can act on it. The ordinal ranking (offset > charcoal > pellet > electric) is uncontroversial and matches our own prose.
adapt.whatMustChange: Drop the decimals. A multiplier invites being multiplied into something, and there is nothing safe to multiply it into — smoke time on a delicate item is a texture/bitterness question, not a linear scaling. Ship it as a 3-band ordinal (`strong|medium|mild`) on `EQUIP_CATS[cat==='smoker'].types`, feeding wood-quantity advice and the existing 'טעם מעושן מדי / מריר' troubleshooting entry (app.js:4758). It must never touch `smt`/`smh`/`sot`/`soh` or any `bcheck` stage — DoD-10.

adapt.why: The user-facing question is real and we do not answer it: 'I have no smoker, show me this on what I own'. E3's `eqvalidity` today can only tell you a path is blocked; O-5's how-to-fix options want somewhere to send you. But the mechanism as specified is a formula.
adapt.whatMustChange: Reject the factors entirely; keep only the intent. Our CP1 spec is explicit: *'A path exists ⟺ its schedule is cited (an oven-only brisket path appears only when a primary source backs its temps/hours). **No formula-generated paths, ever.**'* (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-25-cooking-paths-single-source-design.md:33-34). So a pressure-cooker asado is a new **cited entry** in `sources.py` produced by the research track, surfacing as a new `itemPaths` entry — not `base_time × 0.12`. Note the proposal's own worked example is arithmetically odd: 10 h × 0.12 = 1.2 h, which it renders as 'שעה ו-12 דקות' (1 h 12 min = 1.2 h) — correct by luck, but it reads as a decimal/sexagesimal confusion waiting to happen.

adapt.item: Sous-vide vessel volume as a linear function of weight (§4.5 `meat.weight_kg * 3 > vessel_capacity_liters`)
adapt.why: Our `equipment_map._bath_l()` (equipment_map.py:175-179) is a two-bucket step — `12.0 if kg <= 3.0 else 24.0` — which is crude and has a visible cliff. A linear L/kg model is a better shape, and it feeds a real consumer: `min_bath_l` → `equipment.js:75` `demand.bathMinL` → EQM `cap.baths` fit.
adapt.whatMustChange: The constant. 3 L/kg is uncited, and it conflicts with our own shipped figure of '≈1 ל׳/ק״ג בשר בשקית ואקום' (app.js:2662) — different quantities (bag contents vs bath water), but the coexistence of 1 and 3 with neither sourced is exactly the ambiguity to resolve before adopting either. Also fix the null handling: `(equipment.vessel_capacity_liters || 0)` makes an unfilled optional field throw a hard block on every high-collagen sous-vide cook. Our EQM treats an unknown capacity as 'unknown', not 'zero'.

adapt.why: Our stages carry `kind:'sv'|'smoke'|'dry'|'cook'|'rest'|'bcheck'|'prep'|'note'` (app.js:4093-4169) which conflates *device* with *environment*. A moisture-environment tag is orthogonal and would let a rule reason about crust formation without re-deriving it from the device.
adapt.whatMustChange: Add it as a **derived tag on the existing stage objects**, not as a replacement for the catalog fields, and not as an input the user sets. `kind:'sv'` → `moist:'VACUUM'`, `kind:'smoke'` → `moist:'DRY'`, wrapped-in-foil → `moist:'WET'`. `itemStages` must remain byte-identical in every existing assertion (DoD-10 byte-identity, the same gate E2/E3 passed), so this is additive-only. Drop `FLAMBE` — nothing in our 279 recipes flambés and an inert enum value is a `no-inert-shipment` violation.

reject.item: The Master Recipe replacing our CUTS catalog (§1.1, §3)
reject.defect: It compresses a corpus that has no duplication, and its compression ceiling on our data is ~10% of the CUTS payload — bought at the cost of re-keying 1,008 citation objects.
reject.evidence: `collections.Counter(x['heb'] for x in data.CUTS)` → zero names repeated across 130 CUTS. Byte split of the built CUTS payload: 310,487 total = 189,699 cited (61%) + 59,580 machine-derived `equip` (19%) + 61,208 hand body (20%). Within that 20% body, category-modal agreement is `tgt` 41%, `svt` 43%, `svh` 34%, `soh` 33%, `rub` 19% — so a category-keyed generator is wrong on the majority of the very fields §3.1 promises to produce. Maximum realistic saving ≈ 20% × ~45% ≈ 9% of the CUTS payload.

reject.item: Rule 4 — `IF PROTEIN == "Fish" AND P_TARGET_INT > 60°C -> SET P_TARGET_INT = 52°C AND NOTIFY_USER(...)`
reject.defect: A rule that **silently lowers** a target temperature below a cited safety floor, with no time-temperature basis and no parasite-freeze precondition. It also destroys two shipped recipes outright.
reject.evidence: Our salmon citation (`CUT_SOURCES[49].src.safe`) states: *'Displayed conservative floor 63C (FDA 145F). Salmon served at 50C is below the pasteurization floor — **parasite-freeze (−20°C/7d or −35°C/15h) for raw/rare service**.'* The proposal's rule fires that reduction with only a `NOTIFY_USER` and no freeze precondition. Applied to our catalog it would drive `cut 123` Octopus from a cited `tgt:75` (`'octopus cooked well past that (77C) for texture, not safety'`) down to 52 °C — raw and inedible — and `cut 124` Squid from 63 to 52. Our `safe:63` on all 20 fish/seafood cuts traces to 'FDA cooked seafood 145°F; Baldwin'. Auto-lowering a safety target is the precise inverse of DoD-10.

reject.item: §3.3 cut table — liver at `63-65°C` target, GRILL 220 °C, 4-8 min
reject.defect: Below the poultry floor for an organ our own cited source singles out as high-risk, and it contradicts the proposal's own Rule 2.
reject.evidence: `CUT_SOURCES[71].src.safe` (Chicken Liver): *'safe POLICY — poultry 74°C/165°F (USDA)', url ask.usda.gov/.../safe-temperature-to-cook-organ-meat, note: 'poultry liver floor 74°C; **no SV lowering** — pathogen risk is high in chicken liver'*. Our `cut n=71` ships `tgt:74, safe:74`. The proposal's own Rule 2 says `IF PROTEIN == "Poultry" AND P_TARGET_INT < 74°C: IF method != SOUS_VIDE -> RETURN ERROR` — its §3.3 liver row is a GRILL at 63-65 °C, i.e. the table violates the rule sheet in the same document.

reject.item: Rule 5 — `IF CATEGORY == "Cheese" AND method == "SMOKE": IF P_CHAMBER_TEMP > 30°C: RETURN ERROR`
reject.defect: A blanket rule with a false positive on a shipped, cited recipe. The exception is documented in our data; the proposal's rule has no exception mechanism.
reject.evidence: `SPECIALS n=19` Smoked Cream Cheese ships `smt:110, smh:'1.5-2'`, and its citation (`SPEC_SOURCES[19].src.smoke`) reads: *'**EXCEPTION — HOT-smoked, not cold.** Smoker 200-250°F (~107-121°C), block scored and rubbed, on parchment/pan 1.5-2h until gooey inside but not collapsed.'* Rule 5 hard-errors it. Our 33 cheese SPECIALS otherwise sit at 25-30 °C (Camembert 25 with its own '≤25°C' citation), i.e. our data is *finer* than the single 30 °C threshold — and `SPECIALS n=47` Halloumi carries `grt:240, grillable:true` with a cited 'EXCEPTION — not smoked' note that Rule 5 has no slot for.

reject.defect: It implements neither its own rule sheet nor its own showcase pipeline, and contains at least four defects that fire on ordinary inputs. It is a sketch, not an implementation.
reject.evidence: (1) Rules **2, 4, 7 are entirely absent** from the code and 3 and 6 are partial — i.e. 3 of the 4 pure-safety rules never execute. (2) `target_internal: meat.category === "Beef" ? "71°C" : "74°C"` in `MAIN_COOK_SMOKE`: any Fish or Cheese reaching that branch is cooked to 74 °C internal, contradicting §3.3's own salmon row (50-52 °C) and melting every cheese. (3) `if (equipment.core_cookers.includes("SOUS_VIDE") && meat.collagen_level === "HIGH")` short-circuits **every** high-collagen cut to a 68 °C/24 h bath with **no smoke stage and no wrap** — so a brisket owner who also owns a circulator can never get bark, directly contradicting §3.2's showcase `["STAGE_1_SMOKE","STAGE_2_SOUS_VIDE","STAGE_3_GRILL_FINISH"]`. (4) `meat.weight_kg * 3 > (equipment.vessel_capacity_liters || 0)` throws for every user who left the optional `vessel_capacity_liters` unset. (5) §4.1 says cheese → `RETURN ERROR`; §4.5 emits a `systemWarnings.push`, and only when a smoke tube is missing — so the §12 simulation's claim that cheese 'is blocked' is not what the code does.

reject.item: §1.3's Data Layer — 'ערכים קבועים (Hardcoded) בבסיס הנתונים', sourced to McGee / AmazingRibs
reject.defect: A source tier below our floor, and a storage model that discards provenance at exactly the point the owner's non-negotiable rule requires it.
reject.evidence: CLAUDE.md and `docs/sources/baldwin-backbone.md`: *every `safe` value must trace to a cited primary source — never guess. USDA/FSIS, Baldwin, 9 CFR — not blogs.* Our storage is not a constant but a `{ref, url, note, verified}` record per value — `tests/data-integrity.spec.ts:12-27` asserts every one of 130 cuts has `src.verified` plus ≥1 topic with a real `ref` and an `https://` `url`. AmazingRibs appears in our data only as a *technique/texture* source; it never backs a `safe` floor. A hardcoded constant cannot satisfy that test.

reject.item: §7 Flavor Profile Engine — three profiles (Texas / Asian / Mediterranean)
reject.defect: A ~100:1 downgrade of a corpus we already ship, and it re-specifies scheduling behaviour we already implement more safely.
reject.evidence: We ship **301** seasonings after `build.py:14-18` dedupe (85 rubs / 61 marinades / 54 glazes / 101 sauces; 7 continent groups), each with `ing`, `use`, `origin`, `sub`, a `cats[]` join onto 12 protein categories, plus `flavor`/`base`/`heat` from `seasoning_tags.py` (289) and a 130-entry `house_rub_map.py` giving every cut a default. Glaze timing (§4.2, Rule 3) is already live at `app.js:1287` and `app.js:7272` — every `kind==='glaze'` is scheduled at `lastCook.end − 15 min` **unconditionally**, which is stricter than the proposal's `IF chamber > 140°C` gate. Its 'SOUS_VIDE: אין שמן/חמאה בשקית' also directly contradicts our shipped produce step at `app.js:1534`: 'לצומח מוסיפים שומן לשקית (טעם עשיר יותר)'.

reject.item: Supabase (§9.1-9.3) as the store for the recipe catalog
reject.defect: It moves 639 KB of recipe JSON — 295 KB of which is citations keyed by `n`/`mid` — behind a network boundary, into a merge path that fails silently, for a catalog that is read-only and never user-edited.
reject.evidence: `build.py:87-92`: `_src = CUT_SOURCES.get(_c["n"]); if _src: _c.update(_src)` — a key miss drops the citation with **no error**. Coverage is caught only by `tests/data-integrity.spec.ts` (`expect(cuts.length).toBe(130)` plus the per-cut `src` assertion), and P4 'build assertions + data' is **NOT STARTED** per `docs/analysis/2026-07-27-gap-closing-BIG-STATUS.md` §3.1. §9.1's own justification — 'עדכון גלובלי (טמפ' בטיחות עוף 74°C→73°C) = שורה אחת' — is a use case our rules forbid: a safety floor never moves without a new primary citation, so 'one row, no citation' is a feature we must not have. (Cloudflare Workers vs Supabase as *event/telemetry* infrastructure is a different question and outside my lens.)

impactOnUs:
**If the Master-Recipe model is adopted for CUTS (the version I recommend against):**

- `data.py` `CUTS` (130 dicts, 23-24 keys, lines 5-~500) is replaced by a parameter-set list. Every one of the 130 `n` keys is the join key for `sources.CUT_SOURCES` at `build.py:88`, for `descriptions.CUT_DESC` at `build.py:38`, for `house_rub_map.HOUSE_RUB_MAP` (130 entries, one per cut), and for `equipment_map.CUT_OVERRIDES.get(c.get('n'))` at `equipment_map.py:515`. Re-keying breaks all four; three of them fail **silently** (`if _src:`, `if _c["n"] in CUT_DESC:`, `.get(...)`).
- `sources.py` (415 KB, 4,931 lines): 1,008 `{ref,url,note}` objects across 595 distinct refs must be re-attached. `CUT_SOURCES` alone carries `src.{sv,smoke,safe,grill}` on all 130, `order_svsmoke` on 120, `order_smokesv` on 13 (all with `sv.pasteurize:true`), `grillable` on 130 (25 false), `grt/grh/grz` on 105-118. There is no mechanical re-keying: `order_svsmoke` is a *per-recipe cited schedule*, not a derivable one.
- `equipment_map.py` `apply()` (line 512) currently derives `equip` for all 279 recipes from `casing/grind/cure/smt/svt/age/sear/kg/wrap/somid/rest/coal`. Remove or rename any of those and `cut_equip`/`special_equip`/`make_equip` stop deriving; `stats()['uncovered']` grows silently (it prints a count, it does not fail the build).
- `app.js`: `itemProfile` (3792) reads `c.rest`, `c.wood`, `c.doneness`; `itemStages` (4093) reads `meta.obj.order_smokesv`, `order_svsmoke.smoke`, `meta.obj.safe ?? meta.obj.tgt` for the `bcheck` gate; `methodRules` (989) branches on `isProduce`/`isOffal`/`c.doneness`; `validCombo` (1041); `effectiveSchedule` (4193). All five are on the single stage authority.
- `equipment.js` (441 lines, EQM): `deriveRequires` consumes `spec.min_bath_l` (line 75), `spec.hang` (87), `spec.footprint_cm2` (88); `eqmFitVerdict`/`EQM.availability`/`allocate`/`release` all sit downstream. `casing_mm`/`scale_res` surface at `app.js:7708-7709`.
- **Tests:** 130 spec files / ~788 test declarations. `tests/data-integrity.spec.ts:13` hard-pins `expect(cuts.length).toBe(130)`; `tests/bug3-order-finish.spec.ts:223` pins `expect(r.length).toBe(18)` (the cited post-SV finish set); 83 of 130 spec files reference recipe identity or `safe`/`tgt`; 34 reference specific temperatures. E2/E3's phase gates were closed on an `itemStages` **byte-identity** assertion — a Master-Recipe rewrite invalidates that evidence and both gates must be re-run.
- **i18n:** `lang/_extracted.json` holds **1,536** keys × 6 active languages, enforced by Guard A. Every string the new engine emits must be `L(he,en)` with static literals or the build fails — and the proposal's code emits raw Hebrew literals (`throw new Error("חסימת מערכת: נתח עשיר בקולגן…")`) and raw English (`"Meat will be too tough…"`), which is precisely the v274-v277 leak class. Guard B additionally fails the build on any `°C↔°F` or `g↔kg` drift in a translated value, and Guard D fails on call-site signature drift. Adding an engine that generates ~7 rule messages × 6 languages is ~42 new enforced translations minimum, before any pipeline stage labels.

**If only the ADOPT + ADAPT items land (what I recommend):** `equipment_map.py` gains a `has_skin` derivation and a revised `_bath_l`; `EQUIP_CATS[smoker]` (app.js:34-79) gains two properties (consumption band, smoke-intensity band) with documented derivations; `sources.py` gains optional `loses`/`gains` arrays on path entries; `seasoning_tags.py` gains a `blocks[]` array; `itemStages` gains an additive `moist` tag with byte-identical existing output. No recipe is re-keyed, no citation moves, no `safe`/`tgt`/`svt`/`smt`/`bcheck` value changes.

risks.risk: Silent citation loss during any re-keying of the catalog. `build.py:88` (`if _src: _c.update(_src)`), `build.py:38`, `build.py:94` (`if _mid not in MAKES: continue`) and `equipment_map._apply_override` all no-op on a key miss rather than failing. A migration could ship 279 recipes with a fraction of their 1,008 citations gone and the build would print nothing.
risks.mitigation: Land the P4 build assertion FIRST, before any migration work: `assert` in `build.py` that every cut `n`, special `n` and make `mid` resolves a `src` block with a `verified` date and ≥1 `{ref,url}` topic, and that `CUT_SOURCES`/`SPEC_SOURCES`/`MAKE_SOURCES` have zero orphan keys in both directions. Today this is only checked at runtime by `tests/data-integrity.spec.ts`, which does not run on the Cloudflare deploy path. Per BIG-STATUS §3.1, P4 is NOT STARTED — this is the cheapest de-risking available and is worth doing regardless of the v5.0 decision.

risks.risk: Adopting any of §3.1/§3.3/§4.1/§4.4/§6.4's numbers directly. Not one figure in the proposal carries a source. Three of them are demonstrably wrong against our cited data (liver 63-65 °C, fish force-to-52 °C, cheese >30 °C block).
risks.mitigation: Treat the entire document as a source of *mechanism ideas*, never of values. Any number entering `data.py`/`sources.py` goes through the existing research track with a primary-source `{ref,url,note,verified}` record. A hard rule for whoever executes: if a proposed change moves a `safe`, `tgt`, `svt`, `smt`, `sot` or a `bcheck` stage, it is a spec waiver and goes to the owner in conversation (§4 Waiver Gate), not into a plan file.

risks.risk: Rule-engine messages become a new i18n leak surface. The proposal's code carries raw Hebrew and raw English string literals inline. `OUR-SYSTEM-BRIEF.md` §6 records the v274-v277 lesson: every `he ? hebrew : english` or bare Hebrew literal leaks in the other 5 languages.
risks.mitigation: Any engine module is written `L(he,en)`-first with static literals, extracted by the acorn extractor into `lang/_extracted.json`, and gated by Guards A/B/C/D before it ships. Numeric readouts in rule messages need `dir="ltr"` islands (L13) — a bidi flip turns `≥` into `≤` in a safety warning.

risks.risk: Losing the 400:1 MAKES parameterization by 'unifying' it into a generic Master Recipe. The 102 MAKES are generated by 6 builders + 54 `SG()` calls from ~696 source lines, with per-recipe irreducibles the generic model has no slot for: `casing_mm` (16-120 mm), `calc.salt` g/kg, `calc.cure` type ('1' vs '2') and rate, `rh_pct` (70-80 / 75-85), weight-loss targets (×0.62-0.65), `origin` provenance and PGI history, `sub` substitutions.
risks.mitigation: Explicitly scope any engine work to the CUTS/SPECIALS cook pipeline and leave `MAKES` alone. The `sal-bresaola` citation is the proof case: it records an applied correction — *'Current cure=2 g/kg (~125 ppm) is below the 0.25%/156 ppm standard — raised to 2.5 g/kg'* — a fact no parameter table can regenerate and no generic engine can hold.

risks.risk: Shipping an inert layer. The smoke-intensity coefficient and the consumables rates have no consumer in our code today. `equipment_map.py`'s own design note is that everything is derived so it 'cannot drift out of sync'; a stored constant nothing reads is the opposite.
risks.mitigation: DoD-5 and `docs/process/skills/no-inert-shipment/SKILL.md`: name the render path and confirm it fires on real data before either value is added. For consumption that means the shopping list (app.js ~10049) and the `equipPlan` seam; for smoke intensity, the wood-quantity advice and the 'טעם מעושן מדי / מריר' troubleshooting entry (app.js:4758).

risks.risk: Invalidating closed phase-gate evidence. E1/E2/E3 and CP1 were closed on independent re-audits that included `itemStages` byte-identity checks; 816 tests are green at v277. A catalog refactor voids that evidence rather than merely risking it.
risks.mitigation: Any change touching `data.py`/`sources.py`/`equipment_map.py`/`itemStages` carries an explicit byte-identity diff of `itemStages` output across all 279 recipes × all `itemPaths` entries, as the DoD-10 instrument — the same instrument E2/E3 used. If the diff is non-empty for a safety-bearing field, it is a waiver, not a test update.

risks.risk: `OUR-SYSTEM-BRIEF.md`'s own numbers are already drifting (354 vs 301 seasonings; '279 citations' vs 1,008 citation objects). A decision built on the brief rather than on the code inherits the drift.
risks.mitigation: Correct the brief in place with the verified figures before it is used as the comparison baseline in any downstream plan.

costEstimate:
**Full Master-Recipe migration of CUTS (recommend against): 6-10 weeks of focused work, and it displaces the entire E4 → CP3 → CP4 → E5/E6 → P8 orchestrator sequence.** Breakdown: re-model 130 CUTS into parameter sets (~1 week); re-key and re-verify 1,008 citation objects across 595 refs — this is the dominant cost and it is not mechanical, since `order_svsmoke`/`order_smokesv` are per-recipe cited schedules, not derivations (~3-4 weeks); rewrite `equipment_map.py` derivation inputs and re-run coverage (~1 week); repair 83 of 130 spec files (~2 weeks); re-run E2/E3/CP1 phase gates from scratch since byte-identity evidence is void (~1 week); i18n for all new engine strings × 6 active languages under Guards A-D (~0.5 week). Against a 61%-cited catalog with zero duplication, the return is a ~9% payload reduction on CUTS. That is a bad trade and it stalls CP2, which is already planned, reviewed and waiting on an owner decision.

**ADOPT set only (3 items): ~4-6 days.** Loss/gain path annotations ~2 days (mostly `sources.py` content, and it should ride CP2 rather than land alone); `has_skin` derivation + forced sear stage ~1-2 days; seasoning BLOCK lists ~1 day plus content time. Displaces nothing — all three are additive and fit inside E4's existing scope.

**ADAPT set (5 items): ~3-4 weeks, and only 2 of the 5 are worth scheduling now.** The consumables layer is the one with real user value (~1.5-2 weeks including the sourcing work to replace all five uncited rates, plus wiring the shopping-list consumer); it slots naturally into E4/E5 alongside the already-approved consumption spec. The `_bath_l` linear model is ~2 days. The smoke-intensity band is ~3 days but should wait until something actually consumes it. `P_MOIST_ENV` tagging is ~3 days and should ride the P5a plan-pipeline extraction rather than land standalone, since it touches `itemStages`. Method conversion is not an engineering cost at all — it is a **research-track cost** (new cited schedules per cut per target method), and at ~130 cuts × N methods it is open-ended; scope it to a named shortlist or not at all.

**The P4 build-assertion work (~2-3 days) I would do regardless of this decision.** It is currently NOT STARTED, it is the guard that makes any future catalog change safe, and it costs almost nothing.
